bug_semantics: An authenticated BGP peer can place an IPv4 or VPNv4 next-hop in a crafted MP_REACH_NLRI UPDATE. Before the fix, bgp_attr_parse dispatched the attribute to bgp_mp_reach_parse, which copied the peer-controlled four-byte next-hop into attr->mp_nexthop_global_in without applying the ipv4_martian validation used for the legacy NEXT_HOP attribute, so the route continued instead of receiving RFC 7606 treat-as-withdraw handling. The public first-party record does not identify the later crash, assertion, or resource-exhaustion sink needed to close the claimed DoS mechanism.
flaw_origin: Remote first-party blame follows the vulnerable stream_get through multiple mechanical refactors to FRRouting root import 718e3744195351130f4ce7dbe0613f4b3e23df93, which has zero parents and contains the unchecked MP_REACH IPv4 parser. That is only a remote surviving-object candidate: the bundle-bound clone is vibe-security-radar, not FRRouting, and lacks the candidate and fix objects, so no atomic introducer can be recorded under the clone-binding contract.
